## Introduction
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/getting-started/introduction/
Description: Overview of the Flair visual effects library and design philosophy.

# Introduction to Flair

**Flair** is a modern, lightweight graphics and visual effects library for web applications. It provides:

- **WebGL2 Shader Effects**: 300+ fragment shaders running directly on GPU with declared controls, interactive pointer uniforms, audio reactivity, and scrolling integration.
- **Animated Vector Effects**: 140+ animated SVG graphics, shape morphing, text path animation, and 23 motion primitives.
- **Catalog of Ready-Made Looks**: Over 450 effects categorized and indexed for instant use.
- **UI-Agnostic, Agent-Ready Effect Editor**: Headless editor architecture with Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool bindings so AI coding agents can edit and author visual graphics autonomously.
- **Directing & Interchange**: Multi-shot scene direction with camera moves and export to Lottie, FCP7 XML, and CMX 3600 EDL.

## Why Flair?

Traditional web visual effects libraries either force bloated dependencies (Three.js, Pixi.js) or require hardcoded CSS animations that lack fine-grained uniform control.

Flair maintains **zero heavy runtime dependencies**, works natively with standard HTML5 canvases and SVGs, and provides an architectural boundary designed for pair programming with autonomous agents.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Quick Start
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/getting-started/quick-start/
Description: Get up and running with Flair in under two minutes.

# Quick Start

## Installation

Install `@pixerate/flair` using your preferred package manager:

```bash
# pnpm (recommended)
pnpm add @pixerate/flair

# npm
npm install @pixerate/flair

# yarn
yarn add @pixerate/flair
```

## Basic Example: Mounting an Effect

Mounting a ready-made effect onto any HTML container:

```ts
import { mountEffect } from "@pixerate/flair/embed";
import { loadEffect } from "@pixerate/flair/catalog/lazy";

// 1. Fetch the effect on-demand (lazy-loaded to keep bundles light)
const effect = await loadEffect("fire-border");

// 2. Mount onto your container element
const instance = mountEffect(document.getElementById("my-banner"), effect, {
  controls: {
    uFlames: [1.0, 0.4, 0.1],
    uSpeed: 1.2,
  },
});

// Update controls dynamically
instance.setControls({ uSpeed: 2.0 });

// Clean up when unmounting
// instance.destroy();
```

## Vector / SVG Effects

Vector effects render cleanly without WebGL:

```ts
import { loadEffect } from "@pixerate/flair/catalog/lazy";
import { SvgPlayer } from "@pixerate/flair/vector";

const effect = await loadEffect("hourglass");
const player = new SvgPlayer(document.getElementById("loader-slot"), effect);

player.play();
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Architecture & Design
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/getting-started/architecture/
Description: Architectural concepts, entry points, and boundaries.

# Architecture & Design

Flair is designed as a modular, browser-safe graphics toolkit split into discrete entry points.

## Monorepo Entry Points

| Entry Point | Role & Dependencies |
| :--- | :--- |
| `@pixerate/flair` | Core shader runtime, math, time clock, and transitions. Zero dependencies. |
| `@pixerate/flair/catalog` | Synchronous effect registry with all 450+ definitions. |
| `@pixerate/flair/catalog/lazy` | Asynchronous metadata-first registry (`EFFECT_META`) that fetches source on demand. |
| `@pixerate/flair/vector` | Deterministic SVG frame generation and timeline scrubbing. |
| `@pixerate/flair/motion` | 23 declarative motion primitives (entrances, exits, emphasis). |
| `@pixerate/flair/embed` | High-level DOM mounting helpers (`mountEffect`). |
| `@pixerate/flair/editor` | UI-agnostic effect editor and MCP agent tools. |
| `@pixerate/flair/react` | Thin React component wrappers (`<FlairEffect>`). |
| `@pixerate/flair/svelte` | Svelte actions (`use:flairEffect`). |

## Separation of Concerns

Flair is strictly focused on **graphics, rendering, and scene directing**. It contains no LLM vendor logic or model keys, but exports tool definitions (`FLAIR_AGENT_TOOLS`) so orchestration frameworks (like `@pixerate/ai-core`) can direct Flair autonomously.

## Effect Explorer
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/catalog/explorer/
Description: Search, preview and copy any effect in the Flair catalog.

import EffectCatalogExplorer from '../../../components/EffectCatalogExplorer.svelte';

Search every effect in the catalog, preview it live, switch its presets and copy the code to mount it. Type `#` and part of a tag (`#glass`, `#hover`) to filter by tags, or click a tag on an effect to see every effect that has it; links like `#effects?tag=glass,hover` open the explorer filtered.

<div class="not-content">
  <EffectCatalogExplorer client:load heading={false} />
</div>

## Shader Effects
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/catalog/shaders/
Description: WebGL2 fragment shaders, categories, and presets.

# WebGL2 Shader Effects

Flair includes over 300 GLSL ES 3.00 fragment shaders designed for high performance and visual richness.

## Categories

- **Loaders**: Liquid fill, glowing spinners, flame progress bars, gooey metaballs.
- **Fire & Pyrotechnics**: Flame borders, burning text, campfire, fireballs, burning edges.
- **Holograms**: Scanlines, chromatic aberration, holo projection, HUD displays.
- **Space & Atmosphere**: Star trails, meteor showers, northern lights, clouds, weather.
- **Cinematic**: Anamorphic lens streaks, rack focus with bokeh, bleach bypass, Technicolor, day for night, letterbox bars, academy leader, cinema projector, trailer title slam, dolly zoom, focus-pull and flare-wipe transitions.
- **Beauty**: Skin smoothing, dewy glow, soft focus, lip tint, blush, eyeshadow, highlighter, product shine.
- **Distortions & Glitch**: CRT scanlines, pixelation, ripple, chromatic split.
- **Transitions**: Cross-zooms, light leaks, twister, wipes, dissolve.

## Live Shaders via `@pixerate/flair/catalog/lazy`

To avoid inflating initial web bundle sizes, load shaders dynamically:

```ts
import { loadEffect } from "@pixerate/flair/catalog/lazy";

const effect = await loadEffect("liquid-loader");
console.log("Controls:", effect.controls);
console.log("Presets:", effect.presets);
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Vector Effects
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/catalog/vector/
Description: Declarative animated SVG graphics and motion paths.

# Vector Effects

Flair features 140+ animated vector graphics that run completely in SVG space with zero GPU overhead.

## Key Features

- **Pure SVG Rendering**: Zero WebGL required; crisp at any resolution.
- **Parametric Values**: Modify colors, line weights, and text directly through controls.
- **Scroll & Pointer Scrubbing**: Bind playback directly to scroll position or mouse hover.

## Example

```ts
import { SvgPlayer } from "@pixerate/flair/vector";
import { loadEffect } from "@pixerate/flair/catalog/lazy";

const effect = await loadEffect("infinity-loader");
const player = new SvgPlayer(containerElement, effect, {
  trigger: "hover", // Plays when hovered
});
```

# SECTION: SHADER ENGINE
================================================================================

## Declared Controls
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/shader-engine/controls/
Description: How @control annotations define interactive parameter surfaces.

# Shader Controls & Uniforms

In Flair, fragment shader source code is the single source of truth. Every configurable uniform is annotated with a special inline `// @control` comment.

## Control Syntax

```glsl
#version 300 es
precision highp float;

out vec4 fragColor;

// @control uFlames color [1.0, 0.4, 0.1] "Flame Tint"
uniform vec3 uFlames;

// @control uSpeed float 1.0 min 0.1 max 5.0 step 0.1 "Speed"
uniform float uSpeed;

void main() {
    // Shader logic...
}
```

Flair automatically parses these annotations into structured JSON definitions:
- Control types (`float`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `color`, `sampler2D`, `bool`)
- Default values and boundaries (`min`, `max`, `step`)
- Human-readable display labels

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Interactive Pointer & Trails
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/shader-engine/interactions/
Description: Built-in uniforms for pointer tracking, click history, and motion trails.

# Interactive Pointer & Trails

Beyond Shadertoy's simple `iMouse`, Flair provides comprehensive interactive uniforms for every fragment shader:

## Built-In Interactive Uniforms

- `uniform vec4 iPointer`: XY coordinates normalized to `[0, 1]`, hover progress `[0, 1]`, and duration held.
- `uniform vec4 iClicks[8]`: Circular buffer of recent clicks (XY coordinates, time elapsed, click type).
- `uniform vec4 iTrail[32]`: Historical pointer trail sampled over the last second.

## Example: Pointer Ripple Effect

```glsl
// Distance to active pointer
float dist = length(vUv - iPointer.xy);
float ripple = sin(dist * 30.0 - iTime * 4.0) * iPointer.z;
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Audio & Scroll Reactivity
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/shader-engine/audio-and-scroll/
Description: How Flair shaders sync with Web Audio streams and page scroll position.

# Audio & Scroll Reactivity

Flair fragment shaders can respond directly to ambient page scrolling and real-time audio playback.

## Sound Uniforms

- `uniform vec4 iAudio`: Overall amplitude, bass, mid-range, and treble levels.
- `uniform float iSpectrum[16]`: 64 logarithmically spaced frequency bins.
- `uniform float iBeat`: Seconds elapsed since the last detected rhythmic beat.

```ts
import { ShaderRenderer } from "@pixerate/flair";

const renderer = new ShaderRenderer(canvas);
renderer.setAudioSource(document.querySelector("audio"));
```

## Scroll Uniforms

- `uniform vec4 iScroll`: Viewport scroll progress, page pixel offset, velocity, and scrolling state.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


# SECTION: VECTOR & MOTION
================================================================================

## SVG Motion
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/vector-motion/svg-motion/
Description: Deterministic vector frame evaluation and playback.

# SVG Motion

Flair's vector engine treats animation as a pure mathematical function of time:

```ts
import { svgFrame } from "@pixerate/flair/vector";

// Evaluate exact SVG markup at t = 1.5 seconds
const markup = svgFrame(effectDefinition, 1.5, {
  color: "#8b5cf6",
});
```

Because frames are evaluated deterministically:
- Video/GIF exporters can record seamless loops without dropped frames.
- SSR hydration matches client output byte-for-byte.
- Fast scrubbing along page scroll positions is stutter-free.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Motion Primitives
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/vector-motion/motion-primitives/
Description: 23 reusable animation primitives for SVG elements.

# Motion Primitives

`@pixerate/flair/motion` provides 23 composable motion primitives defined as declarative data structures:

- **Entrances**: Pop, FadeIn, SlideUp, Unfold, Stamp, DrawStroke
- **Exits**: Shrink, Dissolve, SlideDown
- **Emphasis**: Pulse, Bounce, Jiggle, Flash, Float
- **Path Motions**: FollowPath, RotateAround, Orbit

```ts
import { applyPrimitive, PRIMITIVES } from "@pixerate/flair/motion";

const motion = applyPrimitive(baseSvg, PRIMITIVES.popEntrance, {
  duration: 600,
  easing: "spring",
});
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


# SECTION: DIRECTING & SCENES
================================================================================

## Multi-Shot Scenes
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/directing/scenes/
Description: Directing shots on one board, each arranging catalog effects as layers, with catalog transitions and camera moves between them.

# Multi-Shot Scenes

A scene is a sequence of shots on one large board. Each shot frames part of the board with its camera, runs commands that draw or change elements, arranges **catalog effects as layers** over them, shows a title and caption, and holds. It gets into each shot with a **camera move** from the catalog, a **catalog transition**, or both, and the camera can keep moving while the shot holds.

```ts
import type { Scene } from "@pixerate/flair";

const tour: Scene = {
  name: "pipeline-tour",
  stage: { width: 1920, height: 1080 },
  shots: [
    {
      title: "Ingest",
      camera: { frame: ["ingest"], during: "camera-ken-burns" },
      run: [
        { type: "element", element: { id: "ingest", type: "rectangle", x: 200, y: 400, width: 400, height: 280, text: "Ingest" } },
        { type: "element", element: { id: "compute", type: "rectangle", x: 1200, y: 400, width: 500, height: 280, text: "Workers" } },
      ],
      layers: [
        { id: "sky", effect: "aurora", role: "background", until: { shots: 2 } },
        { effect: "lower-third", role: "overlay", values: { name: "Ingest" }, from: 300 },
      ],
      hold: 1500,
    },
    {
      title: "Compute",
      camera: { frame: ["compute"], tilt: 20, in: { move: "camera-whip-pan", values: { motionBlur: 3 } } },
      layers: [{ effect: "image-duotone", subject: { slot: "productShot" }, ids: ["compute"] }],
      hold: 1200,
    },
    {
      title: "Ship",
      transition: { effect: "transition-film-burn", ms: 900 },
      hold: 1200,
    },
  ],
};
```

## Layers

A shot's `layers` are drawn over (and under) its board:

- **What:** a catalog shader or vector effect (`effect`, with `preset` and `values`), a custom shader (`source`, GLSL with `mainImage` and `// @control` uniforms), or a bare picture (only a `subject`).
- **On what:** `subject` is `{ image }`, `{ video }` (a URL), `{ svg }`, `{ text }`, or `{ slot: "name" }` for the host to fill at play or record time.
- **Where:** without `rect` or `ids` it fills the screen; with a `rect` (board units) or `ids` (elements, with `padding`) it sits on the board and moves with the camera. `role` stacks it: `background` under the elements, `subject` over them on the board (the default when placed), `overlay` over everything but the title and caption.
- **When:** `from` and `until` are ms after the shot starts, or `{ shots: n }` for the start of a later shot; a layer lasts until the next shot by default. `opacity` and `fade` (ms) soften it.

The scene tool `find_layer_effects` lists effects with what they take (`{ accepts: ["image"] }`, `{ kind: "vector" }`, `{ transparent: true }`), their controls and presets.

## Slots

A slot is a subject the scene leaves to its host, so one scene plays with any product shot or logo:

```ts
await playScene(scene, board, clock, { subjects: { productShot: { video: videoEl } } });
const mp4 = await recordScene(scene, { subjects: { productShot: { image: "/shot.jpg" } } });
```

`flair scene html scene.json --subject productShot=./shot.jpg` fills one in a standalone page. A slot left out fails the shot that uses it when subjects are given, and is noted otherwise.

A [sequence template](../templates/) declares a scene's slots, with types, labels and defaults, alongside `{{placeholders}}` for words, colours and numbers.

## Transitions

`transition: { effect, ms?, preset?, values? }` names a catalog transition into the shot (`find_layer_effects` with `transition: true` lists them). The last shot's final frame is its `uFrom`, the new shot its `uTo`, and `uProgress` runs from 0 to 1 over `ms` (800 by default). Without a camera `in` the camera cuts, so the transition does the move; with one, the camera moves inside the incoming picture as it is revealed.

## Copies and paths

- `{ type: "replicate", element, pattern: "grid" | "line" | "circle" | "spiral", count, … }` in a shot's `run` draws copies `<id>_0`, `<id>_1`…; `sequence.delayPerItem` staggers them. A camera `frame` or a layer's `ids` can name the copies, or the element's id for all of them.
- `{ type: "path", target, waypoints: [{ point: [x, y], inTangent?, outTangent? }, …], orient? }` in `behaviors` moves an element along a curve at an even speed while the shot holds; a layer placed over it rides along.

## Camera moves

Camera moves are catalog effects of their own kind (`kind: "camera"`), with controls and presets:

- **Into a shot** (`camera.in`, role `transition`): `camera-glide` (the default), `camera-whip-pan`, `camera-punch-zoom` and `camera-cut`.
- **While a shot holds** (`camera.during`, role `hold`): `camera-ken-burns`, `camera-crash-zoom` and `camera-handheld`. The move plays across the shot's `hold`, and the next shot's move starts where it ends.

Name a move by its id, or give `{ move, ms?, preset?, values? }`. `findEffects({ kind: "camera", role: "hold" })` lists them, and so does the scene tool `find_camera_moves`. On its own, `mountEffect(el, "camera-whip-pan", { subject: { image } })` previews a move on a picture.

Camera moves move the scene's camera across the whole board. The catalog's transitions and picture zooms change pixels inside one effect.

## Checking, playing and recording

- `validateScene(scene)` checks framing, timing, camera moves, layers and transitions, and says what to write instead; `checkSceneLayers(scene)` checks presets and control values against the catalog.
- `simulateScene(scene)` plays it instantly on a manual clock and reviews it.
- `scenePlan(scene)` works it out into plain JSON (shots, the camera at every frame, elements, layers and transitions with their shaders or pictures) that any player can draw; its JSON Schema is `@pixerate/flair/schemas/scene-plan.json`.
- `mountScene(host, scene)` plays it in a page and `recordScene(scene, { format })` records it to MP4, WebM, GIF or PNG frames (`@pixerate/flair/embed`).
- `await standaloneSceneHtml(scene)` (`flair scene html`) is a self-contained page that plays it.
- `flair scene lottie | motn | fcp7 | edl` exports it, camera moves included; each format names the layers and transitions it cannot carry in full (`sceneExportNotes`).

## Moving from scene media and effects

`Scene.media`, `Shot.effects` and `Shot.stopEffects` were replaced by layers; `validateScene` says what to write for each. A media shader becomes a layer with its `source` on the shot that shows it, each built-in effect type a catalog effect, `stopEffects` a layer's `until`, and a rig's `media.<id>.<control>` target `layers.<id>.<control>`.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Interchange & Exporters
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/directing/interchange/
Description: Exporting scenes to Lottie, Final Cut Pro XML, and EDL formats.

# Interchange & Exporters

Flair scenes can be rendered directly to popular NLE video editors and web vector formats:

- **Lottie**: Export vector animations for web and mobile runtimes.
- **Apple Motion & FCP7 XML**: Import multi-shot camera scenes into Final Cut Pro or DaVinci Resolve.
- **CMX 3600 EDL**: Timecode accurate edit decision lists.
- **Headless Node.js Export**: High-res MP4, WebM, and GIF rendering via `@pixerate/flair/node`.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Sequence Templates
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/directing/templates/
Description: Reusable scenes with typed slots that a person or an agent fills to get a finished scene.

# Sequence Templates

A template is a [scene](../scenes/) with declared **slots**: a product reveal that takes your product shot and name, a before and after that takes two pictures, a stat countdown that takes a number. Fill the slots and you have a finished `Scene`, ready to play, record or export.

## The format

```json
{
  "id": "product-reveal",
  "name": "Product reveal",
  "description": "A product shot drifts in over a gradient…",
  "tags": ["product", "promo"],
  "slots": [
    { "name": "product", "type": "image", "label": "Product shot", "default": "<svg …>" },
    { "name": "productName", "type": "text", "label": "Product name", "default": "Nova Headphones", "maxLength": 40 },
    { "name": "accent", "type": "color", "label": "Accent colour", "default": "#FF5A36" },
    { "name": "holdMs", "type": "number", "label": "Time on each shot (ms)", "default": 2200, "min": 1200, "max": 6000, "integer": true }
  ],
  "scene": {
    "name": "product-reveal",
    "shots": [
      {
        "caption": "{{productName}}",
        "hold": "{{holdMs}}",
        "layers": [
          { "effect": "mesh-gradient", "role": "background", "values": { "uColorA": "{{accent}}" } },
          { "effect": "image-ken-burns", "subject": { "slot": "product" }, "rect": { "x": 400, "y": 150, "width": 1120, "height": 630 } }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Each slot has a `name` (letters, digits, `-` and `_`), a `type`, a `label`, an optional `description`, and a `default`:

| Type | Takes | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `image`, `video`, `svg` | A URL, a `data:` URL or `<svg>` markup, a subject object (`{ "image": … }`), or `{ "slot": name }` to leave it for the host | — |
| `text` | Words | `maxLength` |
| `color` | `#RRGGBB` or `#RGB` | — |
| `number` | A number | `min`, `max`, `integer` |

**Subject slots** are the [layer slots](../scenes/#slots) a scene already has: a layer whose `subject` is `{ "slot": "product" }`. The template declares the slot's type and label; filling it puts the picture on the layer. With no value its default is used (the catalog's are labelled placeholder pictures, so every template plays as it is). A subject slot with no default, or given `{ "slot": name }`, stays a slot that the host fills at play time, for a live `<video>` say.

**Other slots** fill `{{name}}` placeholders in any string of the scene: shot titles and captions, layer and transition `values`, element text, the scene's title. A string that is only a placeholder (`"hold": "{{holdMs}}"`, `"values": { "value": "{{value}}" }`) takes the slot's typed value, so a number stays a number. Inside longer words it is written as text. Words can be a layer's subject too: `"subject": { "text": "{{headline}}" }`.

## Filling a template

```ts
import { instantiateTemplate, checkTemplate } from "@pixerate/flair";
import { sceneTemplate } from "@pixerate/flair/catalog";

const result = instantiateTemplate(sceneTemplate("before-after")!, {
  before: "https://example.com/kitchen-before.jpg",
  after: "https://example.com/kitchen-after.jpg",
  headline: "Kitchen makeover",
}, { name: "kitchen" });

if (result.ok) {
  result.scene;     // the finished Scene
  result.issues;    // validateScene's issues with it
  result.openSlots; // subject slots the host still fills
} else {
  result.errors;    // a sentence for each bad value
}
```

`instantiateTemplate` is pure and leaves the template as it was. It refuses, all at once:

- an unknown slot: *There is no slot "colour"; "product-reveal" has product (image), productName (text), …*
- a wrong type: *Slot "accent" takes a colour like "#FF5A36", not the words "blue".*
- a value out of range: *Slot "holdMs" takes a whole number from 1200 to 6000; 99 is out of range.*

`checkTemplate(template)` checks a template of your own: its id and slots, each default against its own type and range, placeholders and layer slots the scene uses without declaring, slots it declares and never uses, and the scene's issues with the defaults filled in. `templateSlotSummary(slot)` describes a slot in a line, for a form or a prompt.

## The catalog

`SCENE_TEMPLATES` and `sceneTemplate(id)` come from `@pixerate/flair/catalog`. They are built only from catalog effects, camera moves and transitions. The root entry loads them on demand, so they add nothing to its bundle.

| Template | Slots | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `product-reveal` | product, productName, tagline, price, accent, holdMs | A product shot drifts in over a gradient, the camera punches in to a lower third with its name and price, and a flare wipes to a closing title card. |
| `before-after` | before, after, beforeLabel, afterLabel, headline, background | The before picture, a wipe to the after picture, then both side by side under a headline. |
| `stat-countdown` | intro, countFrom, value, caption, closing, accent | A countdown, a counter running up to the number that matters, and a kinetic closing line. |
| `title-into-tour` | title, subtitle, accent, feature1–3, screen1–3, holdMs | A title card focus-pulls into a tour of three features, the camera gliding and whip-panning between screenshots. |

## Agents

The scene tools (`FLAIR_AGENT_TOOLS`, applied with `applySceneTool`) include:

- `find_templates` `{ text?, limit?, offset? }`: the templates, a page at a time, with a `total` and each one's slots.
- `describe_template` `{ template }`: each slot's type, label, default and range, and an outline of the shots.
- `use_template` `{ template, values?, name? }`: replaces the working scene with the filled template and returns its issues and open slots. A value that does not fit is refused, with what the slot takes, and the scene is left alone. It works inside `batch_scene`, so an agent can fill a template and edit its shots in one change.

## Command line

```bash
flair template list
flair template show stat-countdown
flair template fill stat-countdown --set value=4200 --set caption="orders shipped" -o stats.scene.json --html stats.html
flair template fill ./my-template.json --values values.json
```

`fill` takes a catalog id or a template file. `--values` reads a JSON file of values by slot name (picture paths in it are relative to it); `--set slot=value` sets one (numbers for number slots; a local picture, SVG or video file for a subject slot, inlined into the scene). It writes the scene JSON, and with `--html` a standalone player. Open slots can still be filled when playing: `flair scene html stats.scene.json --subject slot=./file.png`.

# SECTION: EDITOR & AGENTS
================================================================================

## Effect Editor
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/editor-and-agents/effect-editor/
Description: Headless command-based effect authoring and keyframe editing.

# Effect Editor

`@pixerate/flair/editor` exposes `EffectEditor`, a headless editor designed on `@pixerate/editor`'s command architecture.

- **Non-Destructive**: Full undo/redo stack.
- **Keyframe Tracks**: Animate any declared `@control` over time with easing curves.
- **UI-Independent**: Embed into React, Svelte, or run in headless Node scripts.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## MCP & Agent Tools
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/editor-and-agents/mcp-tools/
Description: Declarative tool schemas for autonomous AI coding agents.

# Agent Tools & MCP Integration

Flair treats AI coding agents as first-class users. Every capability usable in the UI or code is exposed via declarative agent tools:

## `FLAIR_AGENT_TOOLS`

- `inspectEffect`: Inspect an effect's controls, inputs, and validation issues.
- `applySceneTool`: Apply modifications to scenes and shots safely.
- `simulateScene`: Run fast, headless simulation to verify timing and layout issues without a GPU.

Refusal messages are human- and model-readable sentences that explain exactly what was invalid and how to correct it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


# SECTION: FRAMEWORKS
================================================================================

## React Integration
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/frameworks/react/
Description: Using Flair in React 18 and 19 applications.

# React Integration

Install the optional peer dependency `react` and import `@pixerate/flair/react`:

```tsx
import { FlairEffect } from "@pixerate/flair/react";

export function HeroBanner() {
  return (
    <div className="relative w-full h-96">
      <FlairEffect
        id="fire-border"
        controls={{ uSpeed: 1.5 }}
        className="absolute inset-0"
      />
      <div className="relative z-10 p-8">
        <h1>Welcome to Flair</h1>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Svelte Integration
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/frameworks/svelte/
Description: Using Flair in Svelte 5 with zero runtime compiler baggage.

# Svelte Integration

Use Flair's ultra-thin Svelte actions (`svelte >= 5`):

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { flairEffect } from "@pixerate/flair/svelte";
</script>

<div
  use:flairEffect={{
    id: "glow-ring-spinner",
    controls: { uSpeed: 2.0 },
  }}
  class="w-32 h-32"
></div>
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


# SECTION: REFERENCE
================================================================================

## API Reference
URL: https://flair.pixerate.com/reference/api/
Description: Complete public API reference for @pixerate/flair.

# API Reference

## Core (`@pixerate/flair`)

- `ShaderRenderer(canvas, options)`: GPU WebGL2 fragment shader runner.
- `ManualClock`: Deterministic frame step clock.
- `blend(bottom, top, mode)`: Color blend calculations.

## Lazy Catalog (`@pixerate/flair/catalog/lazy`)

- `EFFECT_META`: Array of 450+ effect summaries.
- `loadEffect(id)`: Asynchronously loads the effect shader or vector markup.
- `findEffectMeta(query)`: Query effects by text, category, tag, or inputs.

## Embed (`@pixerate/flair/embed`)

- `mountEffect(element, effect, options)`: High-level DOM mount function returning an active `EffectInstance`.
